name: Corradini 2014: LTP primed burst, left temporal lobe, rotating CW (20 min)
origin: Corradini 2014, MA thesis in Persinger's laboratory (Laurentian University), using Murphy's Shiva solenoids and hippocampal 'LTP' pattern
summary: The left-hemisphere arm of Corradini's 2014 memory study in Persinger's lab: the Shiva 'LTP' primed burst stepping clockwise around four coils over the left temporal lobe for 20 min, at the software's nominal 1 uT (not measured in the thesis), between immediate and delayed recall of stories. The thesis reports better story retention after left-sided fields than after sham (4 against 3 people).
notes: Corradini applied the Shiva software's 'LTP' pattern for 20 min over one temporal lobe (left, right or sham: 4, 4 and 3 people) between immediate and delayed recall, on four solenoids per side, clockwise on the left and counter-clockwise on the right (Corradini 2014 p.101-102 [90-91]). Figure 2 gives 1-ms points and 150 ms from a primer pulse to 4 more pulses (p.103 [92]). The other arm is persinger-corradini-2014-ltp-right; the Blind option gives the sham. The vendor's file is not published, so the burst is rebuilt from the figure: 5-ms pulses at 0, 150, 164, 178 and 192 ms (width and spacing read off the plot), five times in 1 s, then 4 s of silence. Rate, pause and the 200-ms step are this project's choices (the thesis gives none, p.101 [90]). The thesis photo numbers the four coils top, back, bottom, front (p.21 [10]); this program steps through them in that order on C5, TP7, T9h and FFT7 or their mirrors, the sites the persinger-collins-gh programs use for the same hardware, with the 5 by 8 cm spacing of Collins 2014 (p.69 [60]). The site names are this project's reading. The thesis says the software delivers 1 uT to each solenoid and names no instrument or place of measurement (p.101 [90]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Reported: better story retention after left-sided fields than after sham (eta2 = 0.60), none after right-sided ones, better word-list recall after either (eta2 = 0.37). The tests are given as F(2,10) and F(1,10), but 11 people in three groups give 8 and 9 error degrees of freedom (p.106 [95], p.100 [89]). Only the scorer was blind, not the experimenter who ran the field (p.104 [93]). Not repeated. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Do not treat this as a memory enhancer. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history, implanted devices or pregnancy; stop on headache or distress.
setting: Dark, quiet room, eyes closed (the lab used a shielded acoustic chamber). Before the program, have someone read you two short stories (and a 15-word list) and say or write down everything you remember right away (immediate recall); run the 20-min program with eyes closed; then recall them again (delayed recall) and score both against the text.
schedule: One session per arm in the original (between groups). For a self-test, run the left, right and sham (Blind) arms on separate days with a different story each time, in counterbalanced order, and have the recalls scored blind.
